title: GraphSHA: Synthesizing Harder Samples for Class-Imbalanced Node Classification

problem.claim: Class imbalance is common in real-world graph-structured scenarios, and off-the-shelf Graph Neural Networks under-represent minor-class samples.

gap.claim: Minor-class subspaces are squeezed by major-class subspaces in latent space, causing failure in class-imbalanced node classification.

contributions.claim: GraphSHA is a general framework that synthesizes harder minor-class samples to enlarge minor-class decision boundaries.
SemiMixup transmits enlarged-boundary information into minor-class interiors while blocking propagation from minor classes to neighboring classes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GraphSHA enlarges minor-class decision boundaries and outperforms various baseline methods across different GNN backbones on seven public benchmark datasets.
The authors report that code is available at the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Class imbalance is widespread in graph-structured scenarios.
The abstract attributes this failure primarily to major-class subspaces squeezing minor-class subspaces in latent space.
GraphSHA synthesizes harder minor samples to enlarge minor-class decision boundaries, and SemiMixup transfers boundary information inward while limiting propagation toward neighboring classes.
The authors report improvements over baselines across GNN backbones and seven public benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: Minor-class performance may be limited by latent-space compression from major classes.

interpretation.claim: For imbalanced graph learning, examining latent-space geometry may reveal a more specific failure mechanism than class-frequency imbalance alone.

application.claim: When addressing imbalanced node classification, consider methods that expand minority decision regions while controlling interactions with neighboring classes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the same mechanism or intervention applies beyond the reported graph node-classification setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the synthesis procedure or model architecture.
The seven benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and quantitative results are not provided.
Independent verification of the reported effectiveness is unavailable from the supplied units.
